# Kevin Lira

> Kevin Lira is a tech lead, engineer, computer engineer, and Ph.D. student in Computer Science at North Carolina State University (USA), working across web performance, SEO, usability, LLM security, automated software vulnerability detection, and vulnerability repair.

Kevin Lira leads front-end engineering initiatives on performance, conversion, usability, SEO, automated testing, internationalization, and scalable web platforms. His research studies practical, scalable approaches to applying LLMs to real-world codebases and vulnerability analysis workflows. His applied research timeline includes TOCA assistive tourism work, SimWear at LCCV/UFAL in partnership with Petrobras, and judicial systems such as CliqueJunte, Cassandra, and Laura at EASY/UFAL in partnership with JFAL.

## Research

- Vulnerability Detection with Interprocedural Context in Multiple Languages: Assessing Effectiveness and Cost of Modern LLMs — 30th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering (EASE), AI Models/Data track, 2026.
  - arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08417
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.08417
- Beyond Code Explanations: A Ray of Hope for Cross-Language Vulnerability Repair — 2nd ACM International Conference on AI-powered Software (AIware), 2025.
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/AIware69974.2025.00017
  - Conference page: https://2025.aiwareconf.org/details/aiware-2025-papers/18/Beyond-Code-Explanations-A-Ray-of-Hope-for-Cross-Language-Vulnerability-Repair

  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/AIware69974.2025.00012
